title: The operation names of the score data product, the rule-in-force read and the case-state read are not published
source: _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T-A.1, T-A.2, T5.1, T5.2, T5.3); Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.5.2 integration points); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench API Specification v4.yaml (/cases/{caseId}/route, /cases/{caseId}/recommendation, /authorise); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.5 DP table, R9)
section: CON s3 Preconditions; s12.1 REST operations provided; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes; s12.9 Call-type summary; s13 | APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow step 3; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes; s13
description: The return-by-route step consumes four rows across four owners and no source document publishes the operation name of three of them: the rwb-source-data data product that carries the per-route COLLINS scores of v_ace_score with their model code, model version, estimate and scored-at time; the rwb-decision rule-in-force and route-set read; and the rwb-case case-state read. Only two consumed operations are published by name, GET /cases/{caseId}/recommendation on the decision base and POST /authorise on the access base, and TSD S1 T5.2 names its cross-module calls as published Java interfaces without an operation name. The baseline and the application story therefore build against a documented use and a placeholder for the three unpublished rows and declare no path, parameter or transport for them.
evidence: The ownership rows of the context pack give S1 three REST operations, no table, no event, no job and one workflow, and name no consumed operation; TSD S1 T-A.1 lists only API-S1-001 on /cases/{caseId}/route; TSD S1 T5.1 is the row 'None'; TSD S1 T5.2 names P3, P7, P4, P5 and P6 as published interfaces with no operation; FSD S1 A2.5.2 gives the integration points as 'ACE (COLLINS scores ingested by ACE; v_ace_score), Model gateway' with no operation; the API Specification v4 publishes /cases/{caseId}/recommendation under x-module P7 and /authorise under the access module, and no score read of P1 under a name.
owner_role: P1 rwb-source-data owner, P7 rwb-decision owner and P3 rwb-case owner
proposed: The three owners publish their operation names before the wave 3 tag; the clients and their fakes are built from the documented use in the meantime, and a published name replaces the placeholder in a minor contract version with no behaviour change.

title: The score element set is given twice and no source fixes where the per-route return is stored after the split
source: _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T3.1, T3.3); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-005 Data table); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (E4 FEAT-VAL-05 row)
section: CON s3 Preconditions; s11 Data; s12.7 Tables owned; s18 Traceability | APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow step 6; s8 BR1; s11 Data; s12.7 Tables owned; s13
description: Three sources read the score three ways. The legacy Data table reads v_ace_score with DF-ACE-270 to DF-ACE-279, an ACE view. TSD S1 T3.1 declares a score entity as REUSE ACE with DF-DEC-019 to DF-DEC-027, carrying model_code, model_version, score_value, estimate_value, route_code and scored_at, and places it beside a valuation table the module is said to own. The ownership rows give S1 no table at all. The higher-precedence reading is that the COLLINS answer is ACE's ingested fact and is read on the rwb-source-data data product, so neither story declares a table or a column of its own and the per-route answer lives in the local decision record until a data owner names a store.
evidence: The ownership rows of the context pack list no table under S1; the legacy Data table lists decision_log_entry, v_ace_score and rule_row and no Workbench table; TSD S1 T3.1 lists score as 'REUSE ACE' with DF-DEC-019 to DF-DEC-027 and valuation as NEW; TSD S1 T3.3 gives score to loan_account and recovery_case by cross-reference; the Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 reads the expected return from v_ace_score, which ACE ingests from the COLLINS models.
area: Data model and ownership, S1 rwb-valuation
owner_role: S1 rwb-valuation service owner with the P1 rwb-source-data owner and the data steward
proposed: The data owner confirms that the per-route score stays ACE's and is read on the rwb-source-data data product, and names the column or the data-product field if a copy is wanted; until then the answer is held in the decision record only.

title: No S1 rule package is in force and no source names the rule that maps the route set to the routes asked about
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.5.3.1 BR-S1-005, A2.5.2 step 1, A2.5.3.3); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T3.2); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-UNI-32 to R-UNI-40, routing sheet); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-005)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 2 and 3; s8 BR2, BR4; s9; s13 Configuration and reference data
description: Both legacy criteria require the answer to be recorded with its version, and no S1 route rule id is in force for this feature: the routing logic carries no S1 rule row for the return by route, and the S1 rule package is Phase 2. No source names the parameter or the rule that decides which routes of LOV-ROUTE are asked about for a case, nor the route-set row that carries them, so the step reads the rule id, the rule version and the route set in force for the business date, records that version and asserts no rule id, no route set and no threshold of its own.
evidence: FSD S1 A2.5.3.1 gives BR-S1-005, that no value a business person may change is written in code and is read from reference data with its version, and states the result is recorded with its rule version; the routing sheet of the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 carries no S1 row for a return-by-route step and its D6 rows are the case states the route decision passes through; TSD S1 T3.2 gives LOV-ROUTE R1 to R8 and no route-set rule; the legacy Data table names rule_row with route_set, from_state and event_code as a P7 row.
area: Rules and reference data, S1 rwb-valuation
owner_role: P7 rwb-decision owner with the business owner of module S1
proposed: The rule and reference-data owner names the rule and the route set of this step and publishes the S1 package; the record then carries their id and version with no change to a criterion, a step or a test.

title: No source names the event or the timer that starts the COLLINS call on a completed ACE batch, and S1 owns no job and no event
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.5.2 step 1, A2.5.4.4); _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T5.3)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow step 1; s12.4 Events consumed; s12.6 Schedules | CON s12.4, s12.6
description: FSD S1 A2.5.2 names three possible triggers of the step, 'a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer', and A2.5.4.4 declares no background event for the feature. The ownership rows give S1 no job and no event, so no Schedule and no subscription exists to start the call when a batch completes, and the only trigger a source supports is the route command that starts RouteDecisionWorkflow. The step runs after the appraisal is accepted inside that workflow, and no timer and no subscription is built.
evidence: FSD S1 A2.5.2 step 1 gives the trigger set as 'a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer'; FSD S1 A2.5.4.4 is the row 'None, No background event'; the ownership rows of the context pack give S1 no event and no job and one workflow, RouteDecisionWorkflow; TSD S1 T5.3 is the row 'None'.
owner_role: S1 rwb-valuation service owner with the P1 rwb-source-data owner
proposed: If the business needs the call to run on batch completion, the data owner publishes a readiness event or the service owner adds a Temporal Schedule covering the business date; until then the call runs inside the route decision only.

title: No published schema carries the per-route expected return on the route operation, and no operation of this service returns it
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench API Specification v4.yaml (RouteRequest, Approval, Recommendation, /cases/{caseId}/route, /cases/{caseId}/recommendation); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T-A.1, T-A.2); Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.5.4.1, A2.7.2)
section: CON s3 Preconditions; s7 C2 and C4; s11 Data; s12.1 REST operations provided; s12.8 Contract fakes | APP s4 Flow step 8; s12.1; s12.2
description: The legacy criterion records the expected return for each route and the route operation answers with an Approval, but the published Approval schema carries no per-route element and no operation of S1 returns one. The per-route answer is published only on the rwb-decision recommendation read, where Recommendation carries expectedReturnByRoute, reasons, ruleVersion and agentVersion. No source says whether the route operation should carry the per-route return, whether the recommendation read is the only surface, or which of the three version elements the record must carry. The baseline therefore declares the route operation as published, declares the per-route element by reference to the recommendation row, and asserts no element name on Approval.
evidence: The API Specification v4 publishes Approval with id, caseId, decision, preparedBy, level, amount and status and no per-route element, and Recommendation with decision, recommended, reasons, expectedReturnByRoute, ruleVersion and agentVersion; TSD S1 T-A.2 gives API-S1-001 as 'Request RouteRequest, Response Approval' with no element list; FSD S1 A2.5.4.1 states the result is recorded with its rule version and A2.7.2 gives the recommendation as a separate feature reading the Workbench and the Model gateway.
owner_role: S1 rwb-valuation service owner with the P7 rwb-decision owner
proposed: The service owner and the P7 owner confirm whether the per-route return is an element of the route answer, an element of the recommendation read, or both; the chosen shape is added in a minor version of the baseline and the record element is unchanged.

title: The FSD names both the ACE score view and the Model gateway, and no source says whether a live model call survives in the target
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (document control change note, A2.5.2 integration points, A2.5.2 prerequisites); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (E4 FEAT-VAL-05 row); _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1, architecture slides 2, 3 and 8); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T5.1)
section: CON s1; s2; s8 BR5; s12.9 Call-type summary | APP s2; s3 Preconditions; s8 BR11; s12.9 Call-type summary; s19
description: FEAT-VAL-05 carries two integration points at once: the ACE view v_ace_score, which ACE fills from the COLLINS models, and the Model gateway, and it declares FEAT-AGT-01 as its prerequisite. The FSD v3 change note re-points the COLLINS scores to ACE ingestion and the feature row reads them from v_ace_score, while the target architecture gives the live model path to rwb-agent (P10) through the Enterprise AI private endpoint. The ownership rows give S1 no external dependency and no rwb-agent operation is published, so neither story consumes an agent or gateway call, and the expected return arrives as ACE's ingested fact on the rwb-source-data data product.
evidence: FSD S1 A2.5.2 gives 'ACE (COLLINS scores ingested by ACE; v_ace_score), Model gateway' as the integration points and FEAT-AGT-01 as the prerequisite; the FSD v3 change note states that SVAF appraisal and COLLINS scores are read from ACE; the Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row of FEAT-VAL-05 reads the expected return from v_ace_score and names the systems 'ACE (ingested from COLLINS), Model gateway'; TSD S1 T5.1 is the row 'None'; the architecture slides give the Enterprise AI private endpoint to rwb-agent and no model gateway of S1.
owner_role: S1 rwb-valuation service owner with the P10 rwb-agent owner and the P1 rwb-source-data owner
proposed: The P10 owner confirms that every live model call belongs to rwb-agent; if a direct call of S1 is required, it is published as an external interface with its contract row and the X dependency of this key is restated.
